sentences.text: So, I'm an AI and Data Science professional.
Right now I'm tutoring at Curtin University, and I just finished a Research Associate role at UWA.
Education-wise, I have a Master's in Predictive Analytics - that's Data Science - from Curtin.
I also have a Master's in Economics and a Bachelor's in Mathematics.
So I've got a pretty strong analytical background.
Now, for my experience - at UWA I developed three research prototypes during my six-month contract.
Let me tell you about them.
The first one was a Multi-Agent AI system using PydanticAI.
It was for mining maintenance data - basically exploring conversational interfaces.
I did 315 commits on GitHub for this, so it was pretty intensive development.
The second prototype was a Neo4j graph database.
This one processed over 7,300 incident records from four mining facilities.
It was all about relationship mapping and root cause analysis.
And the third one was an intelligent Excel processing tool.
It had automatic library selection - pretty useful for handling messy data.
All three were delivered as proof-of-concept, showing technical feasibility with real industry data.
Before UWA, I worked at CIRA - that's the Curtin Institute of Radio Astronomy.
There I built my first AI system - a conversational interface for astronomy researchers.
This was my introduction to LLMs, basic RAG patterns, and working with researchers.
It was a learning project that taught me the fundamentals of AI development.
I also train research students and teach at Curtin - Data Structures, Algorithms, Web Development.
This has really helped me get better at explaining complex technical stuff to different kinds of people.
So why this role?
Well, your mission really resonates with me - improving children's health through research.
That's meaningful work.
The four-month prototype challenge excites me because it matches what I'm good at - delivering practical systems quickly in research environments.
And here's the thing - I have hands-on PydanticAI experience, which is exactly what you're looking for.
Plus I built Neo4j graph databases specifically for relationship mapping.
That's directly applicable to what you need - creating connections between projects, researchers, and themes.
This role combines everything I'm looking for: technical challenge, mission alignment, and the opportunity to make a real difference.
I'd say there are three main reasons.
First, the mission.
I want my technical work to actually have real-world impact.
Children's health research?
That's about as meaningful as it gets.
I've built systems for astronomy and mining - interesting technical problems, sure, but not deeply meaningful to me personally.
Your work directly improves children's health outcomes.
That matters.
Second reason - the technical match.
You need PydanticAI multi-agent systems and relationship mapping through graph databases.
I've built exactly that at UWA.
The multi-agent RAG prototype with PydanticAI?
Done it.
Neo4j graph database with a 12-entity schema for relationship discovery?
Built it.
This isn't me learning on the job.
I can apply proven experience immediately.
Third - the timing and the challenge.
The four-month prototype timeline is ambitious.
I like that.
I've proven I can deliver rapid prototypes in research environments - I did it within my six-month UWA contract.
And here's something exciting - I noticed you're recruiting postdoctoral researchers for autonomous discovery engines.
That tells me you're building a computational biology lab with an ambitious vision.
My Data Analyst role is more focused - mapping research relationships so people can see who's working on what.

But I'm excited because you clearly value AI-driven approaches, and my multi-agent and graph database experience means I can build this mapping system well and potentially contribute ideas as the lab evolves.
